trade_distance.title: Stay in trade range
trade_distance.how: Play beside or just behind a teammate, close enough to swing onto their killer within two seconds. Never more than one corner away from the nearest one.

play_with_entry.title: Pair with your entry
play_with_entry.how: When the team takes space, be the second player in. Your job is the trade on the entry's fight, not a separate angle on your own.

info_before_peek.title: Get information before you peek
info_before_peek.how: Utility, sound or a teammate's call first. A dry peek into an angle you know nothing about is a coin flip.

follow_entry.title: Move toward the contact
follow_entry.how: When a teammate fights near you, go toward the fight at once, crosshair where the killer has to be. Waiting for the call is too late.

use_utility_to_peek.title: Take the first duel with utility
use_utility_to_peek.how: Flash yourself in or ask for one, or smoke the crossing. Take opening duels with an advantage, or let them come to you.

play_the_advantage.title: Play the man advantage
play_the_advantage.how: After the opening kill, slow down: regroup, trade, use the numbers. Hunting alone gives the advantage back.

regroup_after_opening.title: Regroup after the opening
regroup_after_opening.how: Call the kill, take the space it opens together with your team, and avoid a second dry duel.

clutch_time.title: Use the clock in clutches
clutch_time.how: Play for information and time. Take the duels one at a time, from positions they have to come through, and make the defuse or the plant their problem.

use_utility_before_death.title: Throw your utility before the fight
use_utility_before_death.how: If you are likely to take a duel, throw your grenades first. Utility left on your body is money and help lost for the team.

call_your_flashes.title: Call your flashes
call_your_flashes.how: Say "flashing" before you throw, and throw past your teammates' line of sight, not across it.

change_position.title: Change your position
change_position.how: The opponents have read this spot. Play another position on the same site, or the same one from another angle.

change_timing.title: Change your timing
change_timing.how: Same spot, another moment: earlier, later, or only after utility. Break the pattern they expect.

trade_timing.title: Train the trade swing
trade_timing.how: On retake or 5v5 servers, swing right after your teammate's contact, within one to two seconds. Rewatch the rounds above and note when you could have swung.

prefire.title: Prefire the routes you play
prefire.how: Yprac Prefire (Workshop) on this map: clear every angle of your usual routes until no bot surprises you. 10 minutes before playing.

retake_servers.title: Play retake servers
retake_servers.how: Many short 1vX situations: focus on using the clock and isolating one fight at a time.

aim_botz.title: Aim Botz, first bullet
aim_botz.how: Aim Botz (Workshop), 10 minutes a day: 100 kills standing still with the first bullet at head height, then 100 after a counter-strafe.

crosshair_placement.title: Crosshair placement
crosshair_placement.how: Walk the map with the crosshair at head height on every angle, then play deathmatch thinking only about where your crosshair is before the enemy appears.

counter_strafe.title: Counter-strafe
counter_strafe.how: In a private server or a counter-strafe trainer from the Workshop: strafe, tap the opposite key, shoot one bullet. The shot must land once you are stopped.

lineups.title: Learn your lineups
lineups.how: Yprac or a lineup map for the map you play most: two smokes and two flashes per site you play, so your utility goes out before the fight.

pop_flashes.title: Pop flashes
pop_flashes.how: In a private server: practise flashes over the walls and corners you play, bursting before an enemy can turn, and away from your teammates.

v1.title: Joining the Untraded closed beta
v1.lead: Untraded is a Counter-Strike 2 match analysis tool under development. It collects your matches, analyses the demos, and after each session gives you your priorities, with the rounds that prove them. During the closed beta, a few players use it to help us improve it. This text explains what we do with your data, so that you agree knowing what you agree to.

s1.title: 1. What we collect
s1.i1: Your Steam ID (SteamID64) and Steam display name, to sign you in and recognise your matches.
s1.i2: Your match history authentication code and a match share code. With them, our bot account fetches your Premier matches from Valve. The authentication code is encrypted in our database, and you can revoke it at any time in Steam (see § 6).
s1.i3: The demos of your matches, as Valve provides them. A demo holds everything that happened in the match, including the actions and names of the nine other players.
s1.i4: The statistics computed from those demos: metrics, session reports, priorities.
s1.i5: Your feedback (useful or not useful) on the advice, and your display preferences (language, tone, theme, time zone).
s1.i6: A session cookie to keep you signed in, and preference cookies. No advertising or analytics cookies.
s1.after: We do not collect your Steam password, your Steam e-mail address, your inventory or any payment details.

s2.title: 2. Why
s2.i1: To analyse your play: your session reports, your priorities, and how your indicators move.
s2.i2: To improve the tool: calibrate the rules' thresholds, fix errors, and measure whether the advice helps (through your feedback).
s2.i3: References by level: until you have enough history of your own, your session is compared with players of the same level. These references are anonymous aggregates over every player of the collected matches, published only when they pool at least 20 players. Nobody can find your own statistics in them.
s2.i4: With your separate consent (box 2): keep the demos of your matches in a private research corpus, to calibrate the tool and build an open rating model (win probability per round).
s2.after: We do not sell your data, we do not advertise, and nothing that identifies you is published. Untraded's code is open source; your data is not.

s3.title: 3. Who sees what
s3.i2: Other testers: nothing of yours. They only see the matches they played, with the players of those matches, as in a demo.
s3.i3: The Untraded team ({operator}): all the data, to run and fix the tool.

s4.title: 4. How long
s4.i1: Raw demos: deleted from the server {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} after the analysis, except those you agree to give to the research corpus (box 2).
s4.i1Parsed: Raw demos: deleted from the server once analysed, except those you agree to give to the research corpus (box 2).
s4.i1Kept: Raw demos: kept on the server for as long as your account exists.
s4.i2: Statistics, sessions, priorities, feedback: kept during the beta, then for as long as your account exists.
s4.i3: If you leave the beta or ask for deletion: your data is deleted within 30 days, corpus demos included. Anonymous aggregates, from which you cannot be identified, remain.

s5.title: 5. Your rights
s5.i1: withdraw your consent and leave the beta, without giving a reason (in the Settings);
s5.i2: ask for access to your data, a copy (in a reusable format), its correction or its deletion;
s5.i3: ask for your statistics not to count in the references by level.
s5.after: To do so, write to {email}. We answer within one month at most. You can also lodge a complaint with your data protection authority (in France, the CNIL).

s6.title: 6. Revoking access to your match history
s6.body: The authentication code only gives access to the list of your matches; it cannot sign in to your account. To cut the access, generate a new code in Steam: the old one stops working, and we can no longer fetch your new matches.

s7.title: 7. This is a beta
s7.body: The tool is being tested. It may contain errors, in the statistics as in the advice, and data may be lost. The advice is a training lead, not the truth. The beta is free and may stop at any time; we will tell you.

v1.box1: 1. (required to take part) I agree that my matches are collected and analysed as described above, and that my statistics count in the anonymous references by level.
v1.box2: 2. (optional) I agree that the demos of my matches are kept in Untraded's private research corpus beyond the time above, to calibrate the tool and build the rating model, until I withdraw my consent.

auth.label: Authentication code
auth.formatHint: Format: 4, 5 and 4 letters or digits, separated by dashes.
auth.help: On Counter-Strike 2's Steam help page "Access to your match history": copy this code, or create it if there is none yet.
auth.other: This code goes in the other field: it is a share code (it starts with CSGO-).
auth.format: Wrong format: an authentication code is written AAAA-AAAAA-AAAA.
auth.refused: The format is right, but Steam refuses this code. Copy it again from the help page: if you created a new one since, the old one no longer works, so give the newest.

share.label: Share code
share.formatHint: Format: CSGO- then 5 blocks of 5 letters or digits.
share.help: On the same page, under "Your most recent match". If the page shows none yet, play a Premier match in CS2, then come back.
share.other: This code goes in the other field: it is an authentication code.
share.format: Wrong format: a share code is written CSGO-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX.
share.refused: The format is right, but Steam does not know this share code, or it is more than a month old. Take your most recent match's code from the help page.
